propositions: A one-time backfill script samples historical commits and measures cyclomatic complexity and clone counts at each sampled point in time.
Complexity is computed via lizard tool (summed CCN across all functions) and clone_count via jscpd (total duplicated blocks), parsed and stored as integers in snapshots.
Each snapshot must carry a timestamp equal to its commit's date (git show -s --format=%cI), not the wall-clock backfill-run time, to preserve historical trend accuracy.
If either tool is absent or errors on a commit, measure_tree returns None, that commit is skipped and logged, and the backfill continues without aborting.
All written snapshots are tagged with source=snapshot and confidence=high to indicate deterministic tool-sourced origin.
The backfill writes snapshots through the same snapshot.py writer as the going-forward path, ensuring backfilled and live snapshots share one format.
